problem: A 15 kg box is pushed across a horizontal floor with a constant force of 25 N at an angle of 30 degrees above the horizontal. If the box moves a distance of 5 meters, calculate the work done on the box by the applied force.
solution_steps: Calculate the horizontal component of the force: F_horizontal = F * cos(theta) = 25 N * cos(30 degrees) = 25 N * 0.866 ≈ 21.65 N
Work is defined as the dot product of force and displacement, so only the horizontal component of the force contributes to the work done: W = F_horizontal * d = 21.65 N * 5 m
Calculate the work done: W = 21.65 N * 5 m = 108.25 J

entries.target_teacher_response:
The concept we need to focus on here is the definition of work. Work is fundamentally the energy transferred to an object by a force, and mathematically, it is defined as the dot product of the force vector and the displacement vector.

In simpler terms, the work done ($$W$$) is calculated by multiplying the component of the force that acts *in the direction* of the displacement by the magnitude of the displacement itself. The formula is generally written as $$W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d}$$.

When the force is applied at an angle, like the 30 degrees in this problem, only the component of the force that is parallel to the direction of motion actually contributes to the work. The component perpendicular to the motion does no work.

For this specific problem, the displacement is horizontal, and the applied force is 25 N at 30 degrees. To find the work done, we must first determine the horizontal component of the applied force using trigonometry. Given this understanding, what trigonometric function relates the hypotenuse (the applied force, 25 N) to the adjacent side (the horizontal component of the force)?
